The Exalted said:

He is dutiful to his Lord in obeying Him, dutiful to his parents, and dutiful to people by removing their harm and bringing them whatever good he can. ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.﴾ ﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire.﴾ ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense.﴾ ﴿And they will not be absent from it.﴾ ﴿And what can make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿Then, what can make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿It is the Day when no soul will have power for another soul at all, and the command that Day belongs to Allah.﴾

"Al-abrar" (the righteous) is the plural of "barr," who is one whose righteousness is consistently established in general. He is dutiful to his Lord in obeying Him, dutiful to his parents, and dutiful to people by removing their harm and bringing them whatever good he can. He is also dutiful to animals and other creatures in that he does not destroy any of them wantonly or without a permissible benefit. "Al-fujjar" (the wicked) are the disbelievers. "Yaslawnaha" means they directly experience its heat with their bodies. "Yawm al-Din" is the Day of Recompense.

As for the statement of the Exalted, ﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾, some of the interpreters (mu'awwilun) said: this is an emphasis on the report that they will burn in it, and that on that Day they will be unable to be absent from it. Others said: the meaning is that they will not be absent from it in al-barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection). It is as though the Exalted, after informing about their burning in it on the Day of Recompense, then informed about the period before the Day of Recompense, namely that they see their seats in the Fire morning and evening, and so they are witnessing it. Then the Exalted magnified the magnitude of the terror of the Day of Recompense by His saying, glorified is He: "What can make you know," and "Then, what can make you know."

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, 'Isa and Ibn Jundub read "yawmu" with a raised mim (ḍamma), meaning: "it is a day," (huwa yawmun). The rest of the readers, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Shayba and al-A'raj read "yawma" with a fatḥa, as an adverbial of time (ẓarf). The meaning is: the recompense is on a day. So it is a time-adverbial in the sense of the predicate of the subject (khabar al-ibtida').

Then the Exalted informed of the weakness of people on that Day, that none of them can help another, and that the command belongs to Him, blessed and exalted is He. Qatadah said: "So is the Day: Allah, the Exalted, there, no one contends with Him, and He does not grant anyone authority over anything as He granted it in this world."

The tafsir of Surat al-Infitar is complete, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
